transcript.content: Hi, I’m glad you came in. What brings you in today?

I’m here because… my head’s been feeling foggy. I’m having trouble keeping my place in my cataloguing notes at work, even the old ones I know. And sometimes I just can’t decide what simple thing to do next.
Have you been feeling depressed?

Yeah… I think so. Most days lately I just end up sitting at the kitchen table, and it feels like the color’s gone out of things. Even my old watercolor books… they just feel heavy now, not interesting.
Have you been feeling this down nearly every day for at least two weeks?
Yes… it’s been most days. Longer than two weeks, I think. Maybe around three months now, since I started getting ready to leave the library. The foggy feeling’s been there with it too.
Have you been having thoughts that life isn’t worth living, or thoughts of harming yourself?
I… I don’t know. I’ve felt pretty low, but I haven’t really wanted to talk about anything like that.
Have you had thoughts of killing yourself?
I… I’m not sure I can answer that straight. I’ve had dark thoughts, but saying it like that feels… I don’t know. I’d rather not get into the details.
Have you been moving or speaking more slowly than usual?
Yeah… I think so. My body just feels slow. Even walking to the corner store, or sorting papers on my desk, it takes more effort than it should.
Have you been eating much less than usual?
Yeah… less, I think. I kind of have to remind myself to eat. My wife’s noticed I’ll leave rice or soup half-finished, which… I didn’t used to do.
Before this period, have you ever had another time in your life when you felt depressed like this for at least two weeks?
I don’t really know. I mean, I’ve had rough stretches before, sure, but whether it was like this for two weeks or more… I can’t say clearly.
Have you been having trouble with your memory?
Yeah… I have. It’s more like my head feels foggy. At work I’ll lose my place in old cataloguing notes, and then I just sort of sit there, not sure what simple thing I’m supposed to do next.
Have you been diagnosed with a medical or neurological condition that started before these symptoms?
Not that I know of. I mean… I haven’t been told I have anything like that.
Have there been times when the world around you has felt unreal or strange, like you were in a dream?
I don’t think so. Maybe things feel… off sometimes, but not like I’m in a dream or anything like that.
Before this current period, was there ever a time in your life when you felt depressed nearly every day for at least two weeks?

Yeah… I think so. Lately it’s been most days. I just sit at the kitchen table and everything feels kind of… drained. Even my old watercolor books don’t really interest me; they just make me feel heavy.

I’m not sure. I mean… I’ve had low stretches before, but I don’t really know if they were every day for two weeks. I don’t keep track of it that way.
Did these symptoms start after a specific stressful event?

I don’t know if it was one event exactly. It sort of started around when I was getting ready to leave the library… maybe three months ago. Since then the low mood and foggy feeling have been there most days.
Was leaving the library stressful for you?
I guess a little, yeah. I mean… it was a change. I don’t know if I’d call it the reason for everything, though.

I really don’t know. I’ve had times I felt down, sure, but whether it was nearly every day for two weeks… I can’t say for certain.

I… I don’t really know. I don’t think I want to talk about that much right now.

final_diagnosis.reason: Current episode is most consistent with a severe depressive episode without psychotic symptoms: depressed mood and marked loss of interest present most days for about 3 months, with psychomotor slowing, reduced appetite, and cognitive slowing/poor concentration causing work impairment. Recurrent depression was not established because prior qualifying episodes were uncertain. Adjustment disorder was considered because symptoms began around leaving the library, but the syndrome meets a full depressive episode pattern and the patient did not clearly identify the stressor as the primary cause. Organic/unspecified mental disorder was less supported because no prior medical/neurological condition was identified and the cognitive complaints occurred alongside a depressive syndrome.
